title: Recycle Bin or permanent delete - give the user a Settings toggle
description:
UMBRELLA: MPI-526 - Weight deletion and the disk it never gives back (consolidation sweep 2026-08-10). Members and phase order: tasks/MPI-526/plan.md.

SCOPE SETTLED 2026-08-29 - READ plan.md, NOT the older decision below. Fabio: "we can simply give the user the settings toggle for deciding. So if the toggle is off, everything gets deleted. If the toggle is on, everything that can go goes into the recycle bin." Toggle OFF = permanent delete, default. Toggle ON = Recycle Bin with the existing size-quota fallback kept. The trash machinery STAYS and trash@8 stays in package.json - this card adds a boolean in front of what already works.

SUPERSEDED, kept for the reasoning: on 2026-08-09 he asked for permanent delete everywhere, no toggle - "I prefer that they just get deleted, not trashed." That was reversed on 2026-08-29 once it was clear the bin is reachable from Explorer anyway and the machinery is already built.

WHY IT IS INCONSISTENT, AND IT IS NOT RANDOM - this is the user-visible symptom, reported three times. routes/downloadManager.js:305 and :3077 are both trash-then-permanent-delete: _trash() first, and only on a THROWN error does fs.remove() run. Windows refuses to recycle a file over the drive's Recycle Bin QUOTA (the bin cap, not free space - a 6.9GB file failed with 37GB free, MPI-258), so windows-trash.exe exits 255 and throws. Small weight -> bin, space NOT freed. Large weight -> deleted, space freed. Same code, two outcomes, decided by size.

THE DESIGN PROBLEM IS WHERE THE FLAG LIVES: downloadManager.js is server-side and every cross-session setting in this app is localStorage mirrored from js/state.js. Verified 2026-08-29 that the sweep is reachable ONLY from an uninstall (:3109 local, :2956 remote - no boot path, no timer), so one field on the uninstall request reaches both call sites and no server-side settings store has to be invented.

REMOTE IS OUT OF SCOPE: a Pod volume has no Recycle Bin and already deletes through the wrapper.
